summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — CHTR +11%, HONA +9%, SKYD +9%, TTWO +8%, ECHO +7%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (MRNA -7%, FSLR -6%, NVDA -5%, LEN -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: CHTR (+10.61%) — No confirmed Nov 12 driver found. Charter had fallen after its Nov 6 Q3 report (internet subscriber losses, $2B cost plan, Cox integration), so this looks like a rebound or sector move, but I could not verify the cause. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: CHTR is a large-cap cable/telecom name that no strategy's universe includes. A headline-driven jump from a depressed base also would not have passed a trend-following or momentum screen.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed Nov 12 driver found. Charter had fallen after its Nov 6 Q3 report (internet subscriber losses, $2B cost plan, Cox integration), so this looks like a rebound or sector move, but I could not verify the cause.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CHTR is a large-cap cable/telecom name that no strategy's universe includes. A headline-driven jump from a depressed base also would not have passed a trend-following or momentum screen.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap communications/cable names like CHTR to the news-reactive universe, with a gap-up trigger such as a one-day move ≥ +8% on volume ≥ 2× the 20-day average. Alternatively, log it as a no-op if it was a one-off with no catalyst.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found; one search returned only institutional-holdings filings (Quiver), nothing dated 2026-11-12. Likely a technical, sector or flow-driven move, unverified.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (none lists HONA). It looks like a large-cap name, so the exclusion is likely a universe-list or ticker-mapping gap, not a filter. A +9% move with no news is also hard for a news-reactive bot to catch.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a dynamic universe tier that admits any liquid name with a close-to-close gain of at least +7% on at least 1.5x average volume, so unlisted movers get evaluated by the momentum filters the next day.

top_movers.catalyst: no obvious news catalyst found. Searches turned up no SKYD news dated 2026-11-12 and no scheduled earnings or events, so this is likely a technical or sentiment bounce after a weak year.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. SKYD looks like a small or micro-cap with thin liquidity and a volatile price history (about -48% YTD), so universe cap and liquidity screens would exclude it. With no catalyst, a news-reactive signal would not have fired either.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change. A +9% move with no catalyst in an illiquid name outside the universe is noise. Relaxing the market-cap or ADV floor would add more low-quality names than it would catch real movers.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely GTA VI launch-run momentum (Nov 19 release). Nov 9 earnings raised FY guidance and the CEO said presales were 'far in excess of expectations'. I found no Nov 12-specific article, and reported prices don't reconcile.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: TTWO is a ~$40B+ large-cap video-game stock that no strategy includes. The big catalyst (earnings and guidance raise) came days earlier, so a post-earnings gap or momentum filter would have been stale by Nov 12.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap communication-services/gaming names like TTWO to the momentum-trader universe. Add a 'pre-launch event drift' rule: enter on a 5-day return of +5% or more with volume at least 1.5x the 20-day average, if the name is within 10 days of a known product launch.

top_movers.catalyst: no obvious news catalyst — search only surfaced Echo Global Logistics, taken private in 2021 near $48, which doesn't match a ~$101 close; likely technical / sector move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ECHO is likely a small/illiquid name below the cap and volume floors. With no identifiable pre-market catalyst, news-reactive and gap-based filters would not have flagged it either.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a daily 'unlisted-mover watch' that logs names with a close-to-close move ≥ +6% and a 20-day average dollar volume above the liquidity floor, so universe gaps are reviewed instead of silently skipped.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-12. FedEx Freight (FDXF) was recently spun off, and the search turned up only undated items (BofA target cut, Oct earnings, S&P 500 debut). Likely a technical or sector rebound.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. FDXF is a mid/large-cap LTL freight stock that only recently began trading after the FedEx spin-off. It likely lacks the price and volume history that universe screens require. With no news trigger, a news-reactive bot had nothing to act on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a universe-refresh rule that admits spin-offs and new S&P 500 constituents once they have ~20 trading days of history, so the momentum screen can evaluate names like FDXF instead of silently excluding them.

top_movers.catalyst: no obvious news catalyst found. Searches turned up no MRNA-specific story dated 2026-11-12. The listed 250.83 close also looks far above recent ~$30s MRNA quotes, so check the price feed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: MRNA is a mid-cap, high-volatility, cash-burning biotech with no strategy coverage. A -6.75% drift with no gap or news trigger would not pass momentum or news-reactive filters anyway.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-12; likely a sector-wide solar / policy-sentiment move, with FSLR already about 40% off its June 52-week high.

top_movers.suggestion: Add a sector-breadth rule, e.g. when ≥3 solar names (FSLR, ENPH, RUN, SEDG) fall ≥4% on the same day, add them to the mean-reversion watchlist for the next session. No short capability is needed.

top_movers.catalyst: no obvious news catalyst found — searches returned no same-day (2026-11-12) coverage of NVDA; likely a broad AI/semiconductor sell-off or technical move, unconfirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: NVDA is a mega-cap semiconductor that no strategy includes, so no filter evaluated it. A -5.5% move with no company-specific catalyst is also hard for a news-reactive bot to trigger on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add NVDA and similar liquid mega-cap tech names to the mean-reversion universe, gated by a market-cap floor and a no-news check. Otherwise no change: the bot is long-only, so it can't trade the drop itself.
